selectivity.title: Selectivity Analysis
selectivity.tabSelectivityTip: Selectivity View Therapeutic Index (TI), window score, disruption bars, and population lysis probabilities at current field and frequency. The primary readout for judging protocol selectivity.
selectivity.tabMembraneTip: Membrane & Thermal View Transmembrane voltage (Vm), SAR, steady-state temperature, and dielectrophoresis (Re[K]) readouts, the biophysical state variables behind the selectivity result.
selectivity.tabComparisonTip: Preset Comparison How every library preset of the relevant group would score against the current healthy baseline at the current field and frequency. Useful for finding a better target fit without changing the protocol.
selectivity.tipVmHealthyStress: Healthy EP Stress (Vm_H) Resonance mode: target disruption is acoustic, not EP voltage. Vm_T ≈ 0 at GHz (ωτ ≫ 1), so the Vm ratio is uninformative. Shown here: Schwan Vm induced on the healthy mammalian cell by the same RF field delivering the acoustic excitation. This is the collateral bilayer-charging stress on healthy tissue, the physically meaningful safety readout in resonance mode. Rule of thumb: < 100 mV: sub-threshold, healthy membrane unperturbed 100-500 mV: reversible EP regime > 1 V: healthy cells at risk of irreversible lysis
selectivity.tipEthrFull: Target disruption threshold Resonant field at which capsid/cell-wall disruption triggers. Disruption ratio = (E / E_thr) × L(f, f_res, Q) ≥ 1.0 → disruption
selectivity.tipNoGhzResFull: Healthy cell: no GHz resonance Mammalian cells lack rigid-shell resonance, Schwan Vm → 0 at GHz (ωτ ≫ 1). Healthy tissue is unperturbed.
selectivity.tipVmSarResonance: Disruption & Thermal, Resonance Mode T-Disr: capsid disruption % = (E/E_thr) × L(f,f_res,Q) H-Safe: healthy Vm → 0 at GHz, unperturbed SAR_avg = σ_i·α²·E²·wf·dc / ρ (time-averaged, valid in all modes) Use duty cycle to limit thermal load.
selectivity.tipEnergyDose: Pulse Energy Dose [mJ/cm³ = J/mL] CW: energy delivered per second = σ_e × E²_rms × 1 s Pulsed: energy delivered per pulse = σ_e × E²_peak × t_p E²_rms = E²_peak × wf (wf = 0.5 for CW sinusoidal · wf = 1.0 for pulsed square wave) This is the standard protocol dose unit in IRE literature. For cumulative pulsed dose: multiply by N_pulses. At high doses (>100 mJ/cm³), electrolytic bubble formation and medium heating become significant experimental confounders. Ref: Davalos et al. (2005) Ann. Biomed. Eng. 33:223; Edd et al. (2006) Technol. Cancer Res. Treat. 5:279.
selectivity.tipVmSarSchwan: Transmembrane Potential & Time-Averaged SAR Vm = 1.5·E·R / √(1+(ωτ)²) τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) SAR_avg = σ_i·α²·E²·wf·dc / ρ α = 3σ_e/(2σ_e+σ_i), internal field factor wf = 0.5 (CW) or 1.0 (pulsed) · dc = duty cycle Time-averaged SAR drives steady-state heating; T_ss shown in duty cycle control.
selectivity.tipTargetLysisField: Target Lysis Field Minimum E to reach lysis threshold at current frequency. E_lysis = Vm_thr · √(1+(ωτ)²) / (1.5·R)
selectivity.tipHealthyLysisField: Healthy Lysis Field Minimum E to reach lysis threshold at current frequency. Keep operating field below this for selective protocol.
selectivity.tipSkinDepth: EM Penetration Depth δ Exact lossy-dielectric formula (valid for any loss tangent): δ = 1/α, α = ω√(με/2) × √(√(1+(σ/ωε)²) − 1) Reduces to √(1/(π·f·μ₀·σ)) only when σ ≫ ωε (<300 MHz in saline). Saline (σ_e = 1.5 S/m, ε_r = 80, static model): 100 MHz → 48 mm · 1 GHz → 32 mm · 10 GHz → ~32 mm Note: ε_r decreases above 1 GHz (Cole-Cole dispersion); actual δ shorter in practice. ≥20 mm: full cuvette penetration · 5-20 mm: partial · <5 mm: near-surface only Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996) Phys. Med. Biol. 41:2271
selectivity.tipFresRange: f_res Uncertainty Range f_res = v_sound / (2R), uncertainty from v_sound range. Bacteria: v_wall ≈ 800-1200 m/s → ±25-30% Enveloped viruses: v_eff poorly defined → ±40% Tune frequency experimentally within this range.
selectivity.tipQFactor: Q-Factor Uncertainty Q sets the resonance linewidth. Lower Q → broader resonance, weaker peak amplitude. Dykeman & Sankey (2010) validated Q on rigid icosahedral capsids only. Bacterial peptidoglycan and viral lipid envelopes have substantially lower Q.
selectivity.tipBasis: Experimental Basis LASER-VALIDATED: f_res and Q confirmed by pulsed ISRS laser spectroscopy (Tsen 2007-2012) MW-VALIDATED: f_res and Q measured by microwave absorption spectroscopy ULTRAFAST: f_res measured by ultrafast pump-probe vibrational spectroscopy RF-EXTRAPOLATED: acoustic mechanism plausible; GHz RF delivery not yet validated SPECULATIVE: no experimental validation by any method Ref: Tsen et al. (2007); Thakur et al. (2015); Sci. Rep. (2022); PNAS (2025)
selectivity.tipModeBadge: Protocol Mode Selectivity Window DR_T >85%, DR_H <50% Target at lysis threshold · healthy safely below 50% Marginal Window DR_T >85%, DR_H 50-84% Healthy cells stressed, adjust field or frequency Approaching DR_T 50-85% Increase field to reach selectivity window Sub-threshold DR_T <50%, field too low Ablative DR_H >85% Non-selective, both cell types at lysis
selectivity.cmpTipCounterSelective: Counter-selective at current settings: healthy reference DR exceeds this target. Adjust frequency or field.

selectivity.anucleateHealthyNote: Healthy reference is enucleate (no nuclear membrane). NE selectivity is not meaningful as a differential metric.
selectivity.bacteriaSchwanAdvisory: Advisory: Schwan/IRE valid for bacteria, but this cell has published resonance at {fres} GHz. Resonance mode may match the literature protocol more closely.
selectivity.schwanGhzAdvisory: Schwan/IRE model has no predictive value for virus/bacteria above ~100 MHz. Membrane RC charging saturates (ωτ ≫ 1), cytoplasm Debye loss dominates energy deposition, and rigid-shell mechanical modes are not captured. Switch to Resonance mode or move below 100 MHz.
selectivity.tipWindowScore: Population Window Score WS = P(target lysis) × (1 - P(healthy lysis)) WS = {score} (P_T = {pT}, P_H = {pH}) WS = 100%: all target destroyed, zero healthy collateral (ideal) WS = 0%: no target lysis, or complete healthy destruction (unusable) ≥50%: effective protocol window 20-50%: marginal window <20%: poor selectivity at current settings Based on random-orientation suspension probability model.
selectivity.tipPopDist: Population Lysis Fraction with Size Distribution Integrates random orientation (cosθ) AND log-normal cell size distribution. CV = σ_R/R_mean: mammalian ~25%, bacteria ~12%, virus ~8%. For each sub-population of radius r: DR(r) = DR_nom × (r/R), then P(lysis|r) = max(0, 1 − 1/DR(r)). P_pop = ∫ P(lysis|r) × f_lognormal(r) dr (60-pt numerical integration) Ref: Tzur et al. (2009) Science 325:167. More realistic than orientation-only for heterogeneous cell suspensions.
selectivity.tipOrientFrac: Random-Orientation Lysis Probability In a real experiment cells are randomly oriented. The Schwan Vm has a cosθ factor: Vm(θ) = 1.5·E·R·cosθ / √(1+(ωτ)²) For a 3D isotropic distribution, the fraction of cells with Vm > V_thr is: P = max(0, 1 − 1/DR) where DR = Vm_max / V_thr Examples: DR = 1.0 → 0% of cells lyse (none aligned enough) DR = 2.0 → 50% lyse DR = 5.0 → 80% lyse Resonance mode (bacteria/virus): acoustic pressure is nearly omnidirectional , the cosθ formula does not apply. Orientation fraction shows, in that mode.
selectivity.tipDep: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) Clausius-Mossotti factor K(ω), single-shell sphere model. K(ω) = (ε*_eff − ε*_m) / (ε*_eff + 2ε*_m) ε*(ω) = ε_r·ε₀ − jσ/ω pDEP Re[K] > 0, cell attracted to field maxima nDEP Re[K] < 0, cell repelled from field maxima f_cross, crossover frequency where Re[K] = 0 Effective time-averaged force scales: CW sinusoidal: × 0.50 Pulsed H-FIRE: × duty cycle Ref: Gascoyne & Vykoukal (2002) Electrophoresis 23:1973. Note: model invalid at GHz acoustic resonance frequencies.
